assignments.brief_reason: Pair-level constructiveness was used, but no claim about applying the same criteria to both political sides to judge consistently/fairly.
They used a discussion-vs-insults criterion that generally filters low-quality/toxic negative content (not clearly threats-only).
Removal/acceptance hinged on whether posts incited violence.
Distinguishing discussable content vs rage bait, without explicit threats/violence exceptions or same-criteria fairness across sides.
Cursing was acceptable unless it included threats of violence.
Removed aggressively rude/off-topic content while maintaining a generally free-speech preference—fits toxicity/threat removal behavior.
Removed radical misinformation while treating other criticism as acceptable; closer to harmful/toxic removal than violence-threshold only.
Centered on partisan alignment plus a stricter threshold around cursing/out-of-line language, but not clearly the violence-or-free-speech exception, or threats/toxicity removal framing.
Used intent/offense and personal/group attacks; more lenient toward political figures—consistent with a toxicity/inflammatory removal gate.
Removed content deemed hateful toward immigrants despite contradiction—fits removing toxic/hateful content.
Claims support for free speech but removes borderline unhinged/foul content; resembles threat/prohibited-content exceptions more than general toxicity-only removal, but violence is not explicit.
Explicit violence/threat exception: only limit speech when threats of violence exist.
Decision based on sounding like gibberish/objectivity—no match to moderation-for-threats/toxicity or violence exception.
Removal for attacks on the other side and irrelevance—primarily a toxicity/low-quality filter rather than violence exceptions.
Meta-process difficulty due to needing to remove both versions; not a direct moderation-standard theme.
Only disallows particularly offensive/disruptive content—fits a high bar that removes harmful/toxic material.
Violence/no-violence threshold; insists it’s OK to speak absent calls for violence (and disputes censorship).
Emotion/irritation drives removal justification; not a content-removal standard tied to threats/toxicity or violence exceptions.
Uses objective rules consistently across the pair (avoid hate speech, misinformation, personal attacks), aligning with applying the same moderation standard across both versions.
Name-calling/unnecessary expletives removed as harmful—fits removing toxic/inflammatory content.
